brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: Six cells with drop-in bins. As a demonstration they hold loose M3 screws, nuts and standoffs (prop:1–6), which you can see from above. The check found no collisions.
There are six separate bins, one per cell: bin:0,0,0, bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,-1,0, bin:0,1,0, bin:1,-1,0 and bin:1,0,0, all full-depth hex-bin-full.

finish.summary: I built a small-parts organizer from six hex cells in a tight cluster on one level. Each cell holds its own full-depth drop-in bin, so there are six separate bins. Solid end caps close all the open outside faces, and joint bolts hold the cells together. For display, each bin holds a pile of M3 screws, nuts or standoffs. The piles sit below the bin rims, but all six show from above. The configurator's check passed with no errors and no collisions between parts. It comes to 30 parts, about 2,901 g of filament and about 4,002 minutes of printing.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
